post.description: Checks the email and password and starts a web session: the response sets the session cookie. A session the request already carries ends. A wrong address or password answers 401, always with the same message; a body that breaks the schema answers 400, 413, 415 or 422, and no error detail echoes a value it sent. After 10 failed sign-ins in 15 minutes from one address, or for one account, sign-ins from there or for it answer 429 with Retry-After until the 15 minutes have passed; sign-ins still being checked count too. When too many passwords are being checked at once, a sign-in that waited 10 seconds answers 503 with Retry-After.

schema.description: no-store
The session cookie: __Host-tdeemon_session over HTTPS (tdeemon_session over plain HTTP), HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, for the session's lifetime.

post.description: Saves a food, or corrects one: the food with the id (404 for an id the user has no food of), or else the one of the same name and brand, keeping its id; else a new one. A save replaces the whole food: a field left out (a serving, an alias, an optional nutrient, the note) is cleared, so correct a food from what find_foods gave, without its last_use. archived archives the food, or keeps it so; left out, a save brings an archived food back. A name and brand, an alias or a barcode another food has is refused (409), naming that food, which may be archived and so in no search: get_food gives it. Its errors say it as data: where (body.name, the alias's body.aliases[i] or the barcode's body.barcodes[i]) and the food's id as the value. A barcode the user says is a food's is added to its barcodes, so a scan finds it.

post.description: Logs a meal under the client's UUIDv7 (201); the same meal sent again under it is a retry (200), another a conflict (409). Without an id, from a client that cannot make one, the server makes it: that meal sent again is another (or a 409, when its items carry ids of their own), so after a timeout, look at get_day before sending it again. eaten_at left out is the id's time, so a retry has the same; a time still to come is refused (422). An item is a food of the user's by its food_id, or a new food, which is saved, each with an amount in the food's unit (g or ml; a food of the user's takes its own when left out), servings or portions; or an estimate, of a part nobody weighed or of a whole plate. The answer holds the meal with what each item brought, where its day stands (so no get_day around a log), and warnings: values that do not add up, or a meal that looks like one logged minutes before.

delete.description: Deletes a meal, and says where its day stands without it. Its id stays the deleted meal's: a meal logged under it again is refused (409).

patch.description: Changes a meal: when it was eaten (a time still to come is refused, 422), its words, and its items, by ops in order: add an item, replace one, remove one, note one. An item no op touches keeps what it brought when logged, though its food was corrected since; so does an item a note op gives a note, its only change. An add carries its item's id, a UUID the client makes: an add of an item the meal has under its id is a retry when it is the same, a conflict (409) when not. A replace with what the item has already changes nothing, so it does not take a corrected food's values: remove the item and add it again under a new id for that. A remove of an item no longer there changes nothing.

get.description: The plan as a coach reads it: the goal timeline, the targets in force within the last 365 days and those to come, each with what its days came to (the intake against the target, and the TDEE and the rate calibration measures of them, against the phase's planned rate), the limits a change of the plan must keep, the proposal that waits for the user's consent, and the latest revisions. The server computes the outcomes: explain them, do not compute them again.

post.description: Needs a web session: the user's own change of the phases and the targets, in the app. It is a proposal of the user's, made and applied at once: a revision of the plan, which the history shows and a revert takes back, its rationale the code `changed in the app`. The limits hold it as they hold any proposal: one past them is refused (422), each violation an error detail as propose_changes gives it, and so is a change of the past or of nothing. It supersedes the proposal that waits, as any change of the plan does. The answer holds the revision, and what the limits checked, with their warnings.

put.description: Needs a web session: the limits of a plan depend on the profile (docs/limits.md), so no API token changes it. A field left out is cleared.

post.description: Proposes a change of the plan: phases and targets to set or delete, the training weekdays, and the user's limits, with why and the days it was drawn from. Nothing changes until the user consents and apply_proposal applies it; one that changes the limits applies only in the app, a web session. The server holds it to the limits (docs/limits.md), a limit it changes to the instance's and the rest to the limits it leaves: one past them is refused (422), each violation an error detail whose value says the rule, the type of day, the limit, the value proposed and the level that refuses it (user: the user may loosen it in the app; instance: the admin; code: nothing). A change of the past is refused too: a target takes effect from today on, and a phase that has started keeps its type. Else it waits, in place of any proposal that waited, and the answer holds it with a preview: what the limits checked, the weekly average of each target with the rate it implies with the measured TDEE, and warnings.
post.summary: Propose a change of the plan

post.description: Applies a pending proposal: its changes become the plan, a revision of it. Only once the user agreed to that proposal in so many words. One that changes the user's limits applies only in a web session, never with a token (403), and one that loosens a limit only with confirm (409), the user's confirmation in the app. The server holds it to the limits again, as the data or the limits may have changed (422, as propose_changes). A proposal that waits no more (applied, rejected, expired, or superseded: the plan changed under it, or a newer one replaced it) is a 409; applied again it answers as it is.

post.description: Takes back the user's latest change not undone yet, made through any client: a meal, a food, a measurement, a check-in, the notes for a coach. Each undo takes a new UUIDv7 id: the same id sent again (a retry) answers as before, marked repeated, and takes back nothing more; without an id, from a client that cannot make one, the server makes it, and the undo sent again takes back another change; undo under a new id to go further back. Nothing is redone. Changes of the plan and an import's writes are left. A meal logged or changed with new foods is one change: its undo takes the foods back too, whole or not at all. A change that cannot be taken back (an import wrote over it, or what came since clashes with it) is a conflict (409) that says why, and is passed over, so the next undo takes back the change before it. The answer says what was taken back and the days it was of; get_day shows each after it. The web app's undo of a change it just made names that change (last), and takes it back only while it is the latest: after another, nothing (412).
